Algebra I · Lesson 8.2

Which Is Bigger

Solve this lesson →All lessons

Every problem in this lesson gives two quantities and asks which one is larger. The rules from 8.1 are the tools, and the work is choosing which one to reach for. Several of these pairs are built so computing both is slow, and one is out of reach by hand, so the route has to settle the comparison without producing either value.

Problem
Two sums are A=58+79A=85​+97​ and B=59+78B=95​+87​. Do not compute either sum. Work out A−BA−B instead and read its sign. Enter AA or BB, whichever is bigger.
Show a hint
  • Write A−BA−B as one string of four fractions, then group the two with denominator 88 and the two with denominator 99 before anything else.
  • Grouping the eighths gives 58−78=−1485​−87​=−41​ and grouping the ninths gives 79−59=2997​−95​=92​. Add those two results and read the sign.
Show the full solution
Group the eighths and the ninths. A−B=(58−78)+(79−59)=−14+29=−936+836=−136A−B=(85​−87​)+(97​−95​)=−41​+92​=−369​+368​=−361​, which is negative, so the bigger sum is BB​. Both sums are built from the numerators 55 and 77 over the denominators 88 and 99 with the pairing swapped, so they differ by only 136361​.
Problem
Let A=987654×987656A=987654×987656 and B=9876552B=9876552. Both are twelve-digit numbers, so multiplying them out by hand is not the route. Enter the value of B−AB−A.
Show a hint
  • There is no need to compute either number. Rewrite 987656987656 as 987655+1987655+1 and distribute, so that AA becomes 987654×987655987654×987655 plus a leftover.
  • Split B=987655×987655B=987655×987655 the same way, writing one factor as 987654+1987654+1. Both quantities then contain 987654×987655987654×987655, and only the leftovers differ.
Show the full solution
Since 987656=987655+1987656=987655+1, distributing gives A=987654×987655+987654A=987654×987655+987654, and writing B=(987654+1)×987655B=(987654+1)×987655 gives B=987654×987655+987655B=987654×987655+987655. The first piece is the same in both, so B−A=987655−987654=1B−A=987655−987654=1​. Splitting each quantity so that a common piece appears turns a twelve-digit subtraction into a one-digit one.
Key idea
Comparing two numbers is deciding the sign of their difference. From 8.1, a>ba>b means a−ba−b is positive, a<ba<b means a−ba−b is negative, and a=ba=b means a−ba−b is zero. So two numbers to evaluate turn into one expression whose sign has to be found. Whatever the two have in common cancels in the subtraction and never has to be worked out, so A−BA−B can be short even when AA and BB are both long.
Problem
Let A=1249A=4912​ and B=833B=338​. The denominators share no factor, so a common denominator would be a large one. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show a hint
  • 1212 and 88 both divide 2424, so both fractions can be written with the same numerator.
  • Multiply AA top and bottom by 22 and BB top and bottom by 33. Then only the denominators differ.
Show the full solution
Rewrite both with numerator 2424. Then A=2498A=9824​ and B=2499B=9924​, and 98<9998<99, so the bigger one is AA​. Cutting the same 2424 into 9898 pieces gives bigger pieces than cutting it into 9999, so the larger denominator gives the smaller number.
Problem
Let A=915A=915 and B=2710B=2710. Working out either power is a long job, and neither one has to be done. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show a hint
  • 9=329=32 and 27=3327=33, so both can be written as powers of 33.
  • Raising a power to a power multiplies the exponents, the rule from 3.1. Get both exponents, then compare them.
Show the full solution
Both bases are powers of 33. Then A=(32)15=330A=(32)15=330 and B=(33)10=330B=(33)10=330, so the answer is equalequal​. BB has the bigger base and AA the bigger exponent, so neither one of those settles it. Written with base 33, only the exponents are left to compare, and they match.
Key idea
Rewriting both numbers into the same form leaves one part to compare. For two fractions with the same numerator, the bigger one is the one with the smaller denominator, since cutting a fixed positive amount into more pieces makes each piece smaller, so cp>cqpc​>qc​ exactly when p<qp<q, for positive cc, pp and qq. The same holds for powers once both are written on one base, since comparing 3m3m with 3n3n is comparing mm with nn and nothing else. When no common base is available, write both with a common exponent instead.

Neither number of a pair has to be measured against the other directly. Transitivity from 8.1 says that if a<ma<m and m<bm<b then a<ba<b, so choosing one number in the middle replaces a single hard comparison with two easy ones.

Problem
Let A=138137A=137138​ and B=265266B=266265​. A common denominator here is 3644236442. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show a hint
  • Building that common denominator is the long way round. Look instead for one simple number that separates the two.
  • A positive fraction sits above 11 when its numerator is the larger of the two numbers, and below 11 when its denominator is. Check 138138 against 137137, then 265265 against 266266.
Show the full solution
Compare each with 11. The fraction 138137137138​ has the larger number on top, so it sits above 11, and 265266266265​ has the larger number underneath, so it sits below 11. That gives A>1>BA>1>B, and the bigger one is AA​. The common denominator 3644236442 never had to be built.
Problem
Let A=1740A=4017​ and B=2251B=5122​. Both sit below 1221​ and above 2552​, so neither of those settles the pair. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show a hint
  • A middle number settles the pair only when the two land on opposite sides of it, so the one you want is a fraction strictly inside the gap the statement names.
  • Sevenths land in that gap, since 25<37<1252​<73​<21​. Compare each of the two with 3773​ by cross-multiplying.
Show the full solution
Try sevenths. Since 17×7=11917×7=119 and 3×40=1203×40=120, A<37A<73​, and since 22×7=15422×7=154 and 3×51=1533×51=153, B>37B>73​. So A<37<BA<73​<B and the bigger one is BB​. Halves and fifths fail here because they leave both numbers on the same side.
Key idea
A middle number is useful only when the two numbers sit on opposite sides of it. The chain a<m<ba<m<b needs one number below mm and one above, so if both come out above mm, or both below it, that choice settles nothing and another one is needed. The work is choosing mm, and the usual choices are a round number such as 11 or a power of ten, or a simple fraction such as 1221​ sitting between the two.

Two numbers with awkward digits can have reciprocals that are easy to read. The bigger of two numbers of the same sign has the smaller reciprocal, so comparing the reciprocals settles the original pair, with the result read backwards.

Problem
Let A=31218A=21831​ and B=23162B=16223​. Enter AA or BB, whichever is bigger.
Show a hint
  • Computing both decimals is the slow route here. Both numbers are positive, so both can be flipped, and of two positive numbers the bigger one has the smaller reciprocal.
  • Divide 218218 by 3131, then 162162 by 2323. Each division has remainder 11, so each reciprocal is 77 plus a unit fraction.
Show the full solution
Both are positive, so flip both. 1A=21831=7+131A1​=31218​=7+311​ and 1B=16223=7+123B1​=23162​=7+231​. Since 131<123311​<231​, 1A<1BA1​<B1​, so the bigger number is AA​. Flipping replaced a hard pair with an easy one, but the comparison reverses, since of two positive numbers the bigger one has the smaller reciprocal.
Fun fact
Pierre Bouguer printed the first ≤≤ and ≥≥ in 1734, about a century after << and >> first appeared in print. The bar he put under each sign covers the case where the two sides are equal.
Problem
Two numbers AA and BB satisfy 1A=49−712A1​=94​−127​ and 1B=56−38B1​=65​−83​. Enter the letter of the bigger number, AA or BB.
Show a hint
  • Work out 1AA1​ and 1BB1​ as single fractions first, then look at the sign of each.
  • One of the two reciprocals is negative, so the reciprocal rule does not apply here. A number and its reciprocal always have the same sign.
Show the full solution
1A=1636−2136=−536A1​=3616​−3621​=−365​ and 1B=2024−924=1124B1​=2420​−249​=2411​, so AA is negative and BB is positive, which makes the bigger number BB​. The reciprocal rule only applies when both numbers are on the same side of zero. Without that check, 1A<1BA1​<B1​ would be reversed into the false claim A>BA>B.
Key idea
For two numbers of the same sign, the bigger one has the smaller reciprocal. That is 8.1's reciprocal rule, and using it as a tactic means comparing 1AA1​ with 1BB1​ and then reading the result backwards. The shared sign is the condition, and it is not a formality. If AA and BB sit on opposite sides of zero, their reciprocals sit on those same sides, no reversal applies, and the positive number is the bigger one whatever the two reciprocals are. Check the signs before flipping.

A second way to find the answer is to assume it. Suppose one of the two is bigger, then apply the same move to both sides until the statement is plainly true or plainly false. A false ending means the other one is bigger. That finds the answer, and whether it also proves it is a separate question.

Problem
Let A=−(5+11)A=−(5​+11​) and B=−(2+14)B=−(2​+14​). Assume one is bigger, square both sides, and check whether that step can be run backwards. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show a hint
  • Both quantities are negative, so squaring does not preserve the direction of a comparison. Work out which square is larger first, then decide what that says.
  • A2=16+255A2=16+255​ and B2=16+228B2=16+228​, so A2>B2A2>B2. For two negative numbers, the one with the larger square is the smaller number.
Show the full solution
Squaring gives A2=16+255A2=16+255​ and B2=16+228B2=16+228​, and 55>2855>28, so A2>B2A2>B2. Both AA and BB are negative, and for negative numbers a larger square means a smaller number, so A<BA<B and the bigger one is BB​. Squaring is only reversible when both sides are known to be positive, and here running it backwards without that check returns AA.
Problem
Let A=(2m+7)2+3A=(2m+7)2+3 and B=3−(m−1)2B=3−(m−1)2, where mm is any real number. The same one of the two is bigger at every real mm. Enter A or B, whichever it is.
Show a hint
  • Subtract and watch the two 33s cancel. What is left is built only out of squares.
  • From 8.1, a square of a real number is never negative. These two squares are zero at different values of mm, so they are never zero together.
Show the full solution
Subtract. A−B=(2m+7)2+3−3+(m−1)2=(2m+7)2+(m−1)2A−B=(2m+7)2+3−3+(m−1)2=(2m+7)2+(m−1)2, which is zero only if 2m+72m+7 and m−1m−1 are both zero, and no single mm is both −72−27​ and 11. So the difference is positive at every real mm and the bigger one is AA​. Testing one value of mm would settle only that value, while the sign of the difference settles them all.
Key idea
Working backwards finds the answer and running forwards proves it. A chain that starts at a guess and ends at a true statement has its steps in the wrong order, so on its own it settles nothing. The same chain has to be written the other way round, one step at a time, with every step valid in that direction. Adding a number to both sides runs both ways, and so does multiplying both sides by a nonzero number of known sign. Squaring runs backwards only when both sides are known to be nonnegative, since −3−3 and 33 have the same square.

Four routes are available, subtracting, rewriting both into a common form, going through a third number, and flipping to reciprocals. Read the shape of the pair first. Nearly identical pieces suit subtracting, matching numerators or bases suit a rewrite, two numbers near a round value suit a middle number, and small fractions suit reciprocals.

Problem
Let A=1330A=3013​ and B=1534B=3415​. Two routes from this lesson settle this pair. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show a hint
  • One route subtracts over the common denominator 10201020. The other flips both and compares the reciprocals.
  • 30131330​ and 34151534​ are each 22 plus a fraction, and those two fractions have the same numerator.
Show the full solution
Both are positive, so the bigger number is the one with the smaller reciprocal. 1A=3013=2+413A1​=1330​=2+134​ and 1B=3415=2+415B1​=1534​=2+154​, and those leftovers share a numerator, so 413>415134​>154​ and 1A>1BA1​>B1​. The smaller reciprocal is 1BB1​, so the bigger number is BB​. Subtracting works too, since over the denominator 10201020 they are 44210201020442​ and 45010201020450​.
Problem
Let A=718A=718 and B=1812B=1812. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show a hint
  • Neither base is a power of the other, so a common base is out. Look at the exponents 1818 and 1212, which share the factor 66.
  • Write 718718 as (73)6(73)6 and 18121812 as (182)6(182)6. Both are sixth powers now, so only the bases 7373 and 182182 have to be compared.
Show the full solution
Both exponents are multiples of 66, so write each as a sixth power. Then A=(73)6=3436A=(73)6=3436 and B=(182)6=3246B=(182)6=3246, and 343>324343>324, so the bigger one is AA​. BB has the bigger base and AA has the bigger exponent, so neither of those on its own settles the pair.

Every comparison here was between two numbers already fixed. Lesson 8.3, Solving Linear Inequalities, puts a letter on one side and asks which values of that letter make the comparison true. The rules are these same ones, the reversal on multiplying by a negative included.

Practice these ideas

Practice
Let A=1126A=2611​ and B=1129B=2911​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Both fractions have numerator 1111, and 26<2926<29, so 11262611​ is the bigger number, which makes the answer AA​. Cutting 1111 into more equal parts makes each part smaller, so with the numerator fixed the bigger denominator gives the smaller number.
Practice
Let A=59+211A=95​+112​ and B=59+314B=95​+143​. Enter AA or BB, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Both carry 5995​, so subtracting one from the other removes it. A−B=211−314=28−33154=−5154A−B=112​−143​=15428−33​=−1545​, which is negative, so the bigger one is BB​. Neither sum had to be computed.
Practice
Let A=315A=315 and B=97⋅3B=97⋅3. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show the solution
Write both as powers of 33. B=97⋅3=(32)7⋅3=314⋅3=315B=97⋅3=(32)7⋅3=314⋅3=315, the same power as AA, so the answer is equalequal​.
Practice
Let A=2322A=2223​ and B=2124B=2421​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Compare each with 11. Since 23>2223>22, A>1A>1, and since 21<2421<24, B<1B<1, so A>1>BA>1>B and the bigger one is AA​.
Practice
Let A=46×54A=46×54 and B=502B=502. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show the solution
Splitting each product the same way gives 46×54=46×50+18446×54=46×50+184 and 502=46×50+200502=46×50+200, so the bigger one is BB​. The shared 46×5046×50 never has to be worked out, only 184184 against 200200.
Practice
Let A=−16A=−61​ and B=−113B=−131​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word unknown if it cannot be decided.
Show the solution
Both are negative, and 16>11361​>131​, so negating reverses that to −16<−113−61​<−131​ and the bigger one is BB​. Multiplying by −1−1 is the reversal from 8.1.
Practice
Let vv be any real number, with A=(v−8)2+3A=(v−8)2+3 and B=2B=2. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
A square is never negative, so (v−8)2+3(v−8)2+3 is at least 33, and 33 is more than 22, which makes the bigger quantity AA​. Checking AA at its smallest is enough here, since a quantity whose smallest value is above BB is above BB at every vv.
Practice
Let A=350A=503​ and B=467B=674​. Enter the letter AA or BB, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Both are positive, so the bigger number has the smaller reciprocal. 1A=503=16+23A1​=350​=16+32​ and 1B=674=16+34B1​=467​=16+43​, and 23<3432​<43​, so 1A<1BA1​<B1​ and the bigger one is AA​. Cross-multiplying settles it too, since 3⋅67=2013⋅67=201 is more than 4⋅50=2004⋅50=200.
Practice
Let A=337676A=676337​ and B=449897B=897449​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Compare each with 1221​. Doubling the numerators gives 674<676674<676 and 898>897898>897, so A<12<BA<21​<B and the bigger one is BB​.
Practice
Let A=10+14A=10​+14​ and B=2+22B=2​+22​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word equal if neither is.
Show the solution
Both are positive, so squaring preserves the comparison. A2=10+14+2140=24+2140A2=10+14+2140​=24+2140​ and B2=2+22+244=24+244B2=2+22+244​=24+244​, and 140>44140>44, so A2>B2A2>B2 and the bigger one is AA​. The two sums have the same total under the radicals, so the pair with the closer parts is the larger sum.
Practice
Enter how many of these five statements are true. (1) 512>513(2) 210>103(3) −34>−23(1) 125​>135​(2) 210>103(3) −43​>−32​ (4) 1−11>1−6(5) 715<12(4) −111​>−61​(5) 157​<21​
Show the solution
Only statement 3 fails, since 34>2343​>32​ and multiplying both sides by −1−1 reverses that to −34<−23−43​<−32​. The other four hold, by the same numerator over the smaller denominator in 1, by 1024>10001024>1000 in 2, by −111>−16−111​>−61​ in 4, and by 1430<15303014​<3015​ in 5, so the count is 44​.
Practice
Let u=−56u=−65​ and v=43v=34​, and let A=1uA=u1​ and B=1vB=v1​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word unknown if it cannot be decided.
Show the solution
Flip each one. A=1u=−65A=u1​=−56​ and B=1v=34B=v1​=43​, and a negative value is less than a positive one, so the bigger one is BB​. The reciprocal rule needs uu and vv on the same side of zero, and they are not, so comparing the two values directly is the reliable route.
Practice
Let nn be a nonzero real number, with nothing else known about it, and let A=9nA=n9​ and B=5nB=n5​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger, or the word unknown if it cannot be decided.
Show the solution
At n=2n=2 the values are 9229​ and 5225​, so AA is bigger, while at n=−2n=−2 they are −92−29​ and −52−25​, so BB is bigger, leaving the answer unknownunknown​. Subtracting settles it the same way, since the sign of A−B=4nA−B=n4​ is the sign of nn, and no sign is given.
Practice
Let A=2740A=4027​ and B=1928B=2819​. Multiplying both by 280280 clears both denominators. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Multiplying by 280280 gives 7×27=1897×27=189 for AA and 10×19=19010×19=190 for BB, so the bigger one is BB​. Since 280280 is positive, the order is the same before and after the scaling, so 189<190189<190 settles the original pair.
Practice
Enter the smallest integer nn for which 2n>572n>57.
Show the solution
57=7812557=78125, and 216=65536216=65536 is less than that while 217=131072217=131072 is greater, so the smallest such integer is 1717​. A middle number like 105105 settles the upper end at once, since 217>105>57217>105>57, but it cannot settle the lower end, because 216216 and 5757 are both below it.
Practice
Let A=817A=178​ and B=919B=199​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Over the common denominator 17×19=32317×19=323, 919−817=9×17−8×19323=153−152323=1323199​−178​=3239×17−8×19​=323153−152​=3231​, which is positive, so the bigger one is BB​. Comparing each to 1221​ is no help, since doubling the numerators gives 16<1716<17 and 18<1918<19, so both fractions are below 1221​.
Practice
Let A=1245A=2451​ and B=1518B=5181​. Enter A or B, whichever is bigger.
Show the solution
Both have numerator 11, so the smaller denominator gives the bigger fraction. Power of a power rewrites 245=(25)9=329245=(25)9=329 and 518=(52)9=259518=(52)9=259, so 518<245518<245 and the bigger fraction is BB​. A common exponent works whenever the two exponents share a factor, since it leaves only the bases to compare.
